title: The Client-Server Abstraction Barrier & Tail-Recursive Actor State Loops
solutionExplanation: Implements tail-recursive loop/1 with O(1) stack memory and provides clean Client API functions that encapsulate message formats and request-reply synchronization.

otpDocCards.description: Spawns a new concurrent process executing the given anonymous closure and returns its PID.

mentalModelCheck.question: When caller process `<0.100.0>` invokes `counter_actor:get_value(ServerPid)`, in which process does the code of `get_value/1` execute?

options.label: Inside caller process <0.100.0>, where self() evaluates to <0.100.0> so the counter actor knows where to send its reply message.
options.explanation: Correct! Client API functions execute entirely inside the caller's process. Inside get_value/1, self() evaluates to the caller's PID, which is packed into the request tuple so the server loop can respond.

options.label: Inside CounterPid, because the function is defined in counter_actor.erl.
options.explanation: Function location in source code does not dictate execution process. Functions run in whichever process invokes them.

options.label: Inside a shared operating system thread managed by the kernel.
options.explanation: BEAM processes never share threads or execution contexts.
